The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. However, knowledge distillation is not a one-size-fits-all solution; its success depends on careful design choices regarding distillation objectives, teacher-student alignment, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Nuanced Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or teacher-curated data to produce efficient models suitable for constrained hardware and latency-sensitive applications. Its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data or privacy constraints, and complementing KD with task-aware architecture choices, robustness-aware training, or pruning and quantization. KD can markedly reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but it requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors or losing rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Gill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD techniques—ranging from soft-target matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, and data-side strategies—have enabled effective compression across vision, speech, language, and graph domains. At the same time, empirical work shows KD is most successful when integrated into engineered pipelines that match distillation signals to student capacity, address data limitations, and explicitly manage robustness and task-specific constraints. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central but context-sensitive component of compression toolkits and gives concrete recommendations for practitioners seeking reliable, deployable student models.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more specialized models while retaining much of the original performance. The approaches span matching teacher soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mapping, data augmentation during transfer, data-free distillation, and architecture-aware compression. Practical systems combine distillation with neural architecture search, federated or privacy-preserving protocols, and multimodal adaptation to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, heterogeneity of devices, and absence of original training data. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical insights, and deployment-oriented strategies developed to date.

papers_seen.author: Lynn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student. A broad family of KD methods—including matching teacher output distributions, imitating intermediate features or attention maps, multi-teacher and online schemes, and teacher-free/self-distillation variants—has been developed and frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can retain much of teacher performance when distillation targets, representation alignment, and data strategies are chosen to suit student capacity and task structure. Key practical issues include selecting appropriate transfer signals, handling limited or private data, and diagnosing failures under distribution shift and long-tail phenomena. Remaining research directions emphasize principled teacher–student alignment, robust distillation under domain shift and data scarcity, and automated, task-aware compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Gallegos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile compression approach that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of task performance. KD operates at multiple levels (logits, features, intermediate layers), admits data-aware and data-free variants, and is most effective when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful teacher–student co‑design. However, KD is not a universal silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, task specifics, and optimization choices. Practitioners should treat KD as a central tool in a broader, task‑aware compression pipeline that explicitly accounts for these limitations.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Glass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Composable, and Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a composable element in integrated compression pipelines, KD enables substantial reductions in inference latency, memory footprint, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. Realizing KD's benefits in production requires task-aware objectives, careful teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data approaches), and explicit attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Austin
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. It is a flexible toolkit that operates at multiple levels (outputs, internal representations, attention/relations) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distillation variants address different deployment constraints — e.g., privacy, communication, or missing original data — and have been applied across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized tasks. Practical success requires careful teacher–student alignment, task-aware choices about what to transfer, and realistic evaluation for robustness and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Mccarty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical default for compressing large models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. As a flexible, composable toolkit, KD can transfer output behavior, internal representations, and relational structure; it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation; and it supports data-aware strategies for privacy- or data-constrained settings. Realizing its benefits requires deliberate choices about distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and handling of domain shift or teacher errors, but when applied as an engineering-first, context-sensitive framework KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs for production deployments.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—such as softened logits, intermediate representations, and relational signals—and is typically integrated with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, and speech tasks, but practical success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, data choices, and explicit evaluation of robustness, privacy, and long-tail behavior. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, reliable distillation with limited or private data, and preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors under compression.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A spectrum of techniques—from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free strategies—enables practical reductions in model size, memory, and latency across vision, NLP, graph, and reinforcement-learning applications. Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals and student capacity, managing data availability and privacy, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, softened outputs, intermediate representations, or synthesized signals. KD is widely applied across computer vision, speech, and natural language processing to reduce parameter counts, inference latency, and memory usage while preserving much of teacher performance. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to handle data availability and privacy constraints, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization). KD is a versatile, composable tool for deployment but not a universal remedy: deployment requires task‑aware design, attention to robustness and rare‑token behavior, and ongoing evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Dougherty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring information from large ‘‘teacher’’ models into smaller ‘‘student’’ models to reduce storage, latency, and compute while retaining much of the teacher’s task performance. KD techniques include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multiple teachers or online schemes, and operating without original training data. In practice KD is often used within broader compression pipelines that include pruning, quantization, and architecture design; its effectiveness depends on teacher–student design, data availability, and attention to robustness, fairness, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for compressing neural networks and transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including neural machine translation, language models, graph neural networks, and speech processing. The technique enables deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy through various knowledge transfer mechanisms and distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible means of producing compact student models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD is not a single algorithm but a configurable toolkit—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention mimicry, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free procedures—that, when matched to task constraints and combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), reliably improves deployability in latency-, memory-, energy- and privacy-constrained environments. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires deliberate teacher–student design, careful data strategies (including handling limited or private data), attention to robustness and transferred failure modes, and empirical validation under deployment distributions. I argue KD should be the default starting point in compression pipelines, applied in a task-aware and composable way rather than as a one-size-fits-all cure.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. Over the past decade KD evolved from matching soft logits into a broad set of techniques—feature-level and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, curriculum and architecture-aware strategies—that collectively enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation objectives, data regimes, and student architectures to deployment constraints; open issues include teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Complementary Techniques, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into efficient students suitable for deployment. KD is versatile: it transfers logits, intermediate representations, and relational knowledge, can operate with or without original training data, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real-world constraints. However, distilled models can inherit optimization difficulties, dataset artifacts, and biases from teachers, so reliable deployment requires task-adaptive method design, student-aware objectives, and privacy- or resource-aware protocols. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables production-ready compression across vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Mejia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints in deep learning and NLP. KD methods reduce model size, inference latency, and memory cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression primitives. When applied as a configurable component of a compression pipeline, KD delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs while posing open challenges around robustness, fairness, and data- or privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential and Context-Dependent Framework for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to students through multiple mechanisms—including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and multi-teacher strategies—knowledge distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. However, distillation is neither universal nor automatic; its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge is transferred, data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, and integration with complementary compression methods. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a central but context-dependent toolkit requiring thoughtful application, task-aware adaptation, and combination with other compression strategies to achieve production-ready results.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher networks to compact student networks, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from soft-target matching to feature alignment and data-free approaches, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and multimodal tasks. Effective knowledge distillation requires careful consideration of distillation targets, data availability, teacher quality, and student-teacher architectural alignment to achieve optimal compression and performance trade-offs in real-world deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Tradeoffs, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practically oriented family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Methods include output-level soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, progressive module replacement, and self- or online-distillation; KD is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical work shows strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision and language tasks, but outcomes depend on teacher–student design, the choice of distillation signal, data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and concerns about robustness and transferred artifacts. Important open problems remain in principled target selection, reliable transfer under domain shift, and automated, task-aware compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Core Principles and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks through various mechanisms, enabling significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has evolved into a comprehensive toolkit encompassing multiple methodologies and has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation.

papers_seen.author: Matthews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to student networks, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. This approach encompasses diverse methodologies and has demonstrated broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it an indispensable method for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models that can be deployed on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models, addressing critical deployment challenges across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. By combining diverse methodological approaches and complementary compression techniques, knowledge distillation enables practical solutions for real-world systems requiring efficient inference, reduced memory consumption, and faster computation without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds in diverse settings when treated as a composable toolkit—combining output-level supervision, representation-level imitation, curriculum and multi-teacher strategies, and complementary compression methods. Its value is strongest in real-world deployments that demand low latency, limited memory, privacy constraints, or device heterogeneity, though careful design choices are required to avoid transferring teacher errors or exacerbating robustness and domain-shift issues.

papers_seen.author: Bradley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models by transferring information from high-capacity teacher models. Rather than a single algorithmic approach, KD functions as a flexible, composable framework that combines multiple complementary mechanisms—including soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, attention alignment, and data-aware strategies—to address practical deployment constraints such as latency, memory efficiency, and privacy preservation. When properly designed and adapted to task, data, and hardware requirements, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of the teacher's performance across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a foundational model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment of neural networks in resource-constrained environments. The field has evolved from simple soft-target matching to sophisticated multi-level knowledge transfer strategies, encompassing diverse approaches including intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free methods, and task-aware adaptations. Knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size, latency, and computational cost while preserving competitive performance across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and other domains. However, practical success depends on careful design choices regarding teacher selection, the choice of distilled signals, student capacity, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and natural language processing systems in computationally limited environments. This approach encompasses diverse methodologies and mechanisms that address critical real-world deployment challenges including inference latency, memory efficiency, computational cost, and privacy preservation, with broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be the default starting point for compressing large deep models into deployable students because it combines empirical effectiveness, methodological flexibility, and natural compatibility with other compression techniques. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), enables substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving performance, and has been demonstrated across modalities including NLP. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play remedy: success depends on deliberate teacher–student alignment, data strategy, careful selection of distilled signals, and attention to robustness and undesirable behavior transfer. Practitioners should adopt KD as a first-line tool while pairing it with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and evaluation practices tailored to target constraints and risks.

papers_seen.author: Mccarty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical default for compressing large models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. As a flexible, composable toolkit, KD can transfer output behavior, internal representations, and relational structure; it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation; and it supports data-aware strategies for privacy- or data-constrained settings. Realizing its benefits requires deliberate choices about distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and handling of domain shift or teacher errors, but when applied as an engineering-first, context-sensitive framework KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs for production deployments.

While distillation routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer; attention to optimization dynamics, robustness, and bias transfer is necessary for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models, achieving substantial reductions in parameters, memory consumption, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. The field encompasses diverse methodologies and has been successfully applied across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains. Practical success requires careful design choices regarding what signals to transfer, how to align teacher-student architectures, and how to manage data availability and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while preserving much of the teacher's performance. Rather than a single monolithic method, KD represents a flexible, composable framework that transfers knowledge through multiple complementary mechanisms. The field encompasses diverse approaches for selecting transfer targets, aligning architectures, handling data constraints, and integrating with complementary compression techniques. While KD has demonstrated broad empirical effectiveness across vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, practical success depends critically on careful design choices, task-aware adaptation, and attention to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and recommendation systems. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple complementary strategies and, when carefully designed and integrated with other compression techniques, provides essential solutions for reducing model size, inference latency, and memory consumption in real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Wallace
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical framework for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and representational structure. KD techniques span softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer- and token-wise supervision, online or multi-teacher schemes, and data-centric strategies (including synthetic or data-free distillation). In practice KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when teacher–student design, training objectives, and data regimes are chosen to match deployment constraints and robustness goals.

papers_seen.author: Mckinney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD has evolved into a multi-signal toolkit—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, layer-wise and relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-side strategies including synthetic or privacy-preserving data—that, when combined with complementary compression methods, yields practical reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective use requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data strategies (including pretraining and data-free methods), and evaluation under distributional and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models by transferring information from higher-capacity teacher models. Methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and extend to self-distillation, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free or few-shot workflows, and privacy-aware compression. Distillation is widely applied in vision, language, speech, and multimodal systems to reduce latency, memory, and energy use while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Empirical work shows distillation can improve inference efficiency, sometimes aid generalization, and enable robust or privacy-preserving deployment when combined with complementary compression techniques; however, challenges remain in teacher–student mismatch, sensitivity to data regimes, representation alignment, fairness and privacy guarantees, and principled theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the creation of efficient student models that learn from larger, more complex teacher networks. This approach addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The methodology spans multiple domains including computer vision, NLP tasks, and graph neural networks, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness across different problem spaces. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation has been extended to address important concerns such as adversarial robustness, privacy preservation, fairness mitigation, and domain generalization, establishing it as a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive neural networks (teacher models) to smaller, more efficient student models. These methods address critical practical deployment constraints including inference latency, memory consumption, computational efficiency, and device heterogeneity while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation mechanisms span multiple approaches—from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate feature and layer-level alignment—and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The field encompasses diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, serving as a central, versatile toolkit for enabling efficient model deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized training signals so compact systems can meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. A diverse toolkit—soft-label matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-side strategies including augmentation or synthetic/example-free distillation—has been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search in practice. Success depends on selecting which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and preparing appropriate data; remaining challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, reducing dependence on original training data, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors, and better principled teacher design for specific student and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large-scale deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while preserving competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when carefully applied with attention to task-specific requirements and design choices, represents a vital strategy for enabling practical real-world deployment of neural networks across diverse domains and applications.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models. KD enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and resource use while often preserving strong task performance. However, its practical value depends on careful choice of teacher signals, student capacity, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques; when applied thoughtfully, KD supports privacy-preserving, domain-adaptive, and hardware-aware deployment of compact models, but it is not a one-size-fits-all solution and must be integrated into broader compression and robustness workflows.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven approach for compressing large neural networks into efficient models suitable for deployment. Across modalities and tasks — from vision and speech to NLP and retrieval — KD can be implemented through multiple, complementary mechanisms (soft-label supervision, feature mimicry, layer-wise alignment, teacher adaptation, and online co-training) to trade off capacity, compute, and data constraints while retaining much of the teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines benefit from task-aware selection of distilled signals, efficient label generation or online schemes to reduce teacher cost, and teacher/student co-design to close the capacity gap between models.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Task-Aware Core for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable component within broader compression pipelines—together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search—and adapted to task constraints and data regimes, KD yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, reliable deployment requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, data availability and distribution shift, and targeted evaluation of robustness and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Cervantes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across deep learning and NLP, KD has evolved from matching soft teacher outputs to a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-representation transfer, layer-wise and task-aware methods, self-distillation, and composition with pruning or quantization. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance, but practical deployment requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. Open challenges include reliably transferring structural or rare behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and automated, task-aware pipelines for heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unified Tool for Model Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking models: it is a flexible family of techniques that enables compression, privacy-preserving transfer, robustness under limited data, and improved task- or domain-specific performance. By transferring behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students, KD enables deployment of performant models in constrained environments while enabling adaptations such as data-free distillation, task-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware transfers. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary engineering and research lever for model compression across modalities and tasks, and outlines practical variants that address common deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Christensen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful design choices tailored to specific deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the predictive capacity of larger teachers. When applied as a deliberate, task-aware element within a broader compression pipeline (including pretraining, pruning, and quantization), KD enables deployment under real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its many instantiations—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention- or layer-aware mappings, and multi-teacher or data-centric variants—make KD the recommended default starting point for model compression, provided designers attend to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, and dataset/regime-specific caveats.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central technique in model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD routinely delivers strong size–performance trade-offs by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate structure from large teachers to compact students, and it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real deployment constraints. Realizing KD’s benefits in production requires context-sensitive design: align teacher and student capacity, choose distillation targets suited to the task, handle limited or private data with specialized methods, and evaluate robustness and distributional generalization. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables practical, deployable models that balance accuracy, latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment of sophisticated deep learning and NLP systems across diverse domains. The technique encompasses multiple complementary strategies ranging from soft-label matching and feature-level transfer to data-aware and data-free variants. When treated as a central, composable component of compression pipelines and combined with careful design choices, knowledge distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while often preserving much of the teacher's performance.

papers_seen.author: Tyler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Deployment Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning and NLP systems on devices with limited computational resources. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies and has demonstrated broad applicability across vision, language, and specialized domains, addressing critical challenges including inference latency, memory consumption, computational efficiency, and privacy preservation.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent essential techniques for deploying sophisticated deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable large, high-performing teacher models to transfer their learned knowledge to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the computational and memory limitations that prevent state-of-the-art systems from reaching practical applications. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Myers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems across diverse domains. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms, design principles, complementary techniques, and practical considerations essential for effective model compression in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, achieving substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized tasks. Knowledge distillation should be understood as a flexible, composable toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all solution, requiring careful consideration of what knowledge to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including reduced latency, memory footprint, and computational cost across diverse domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. However, effective distillation requires careful orchestration of multiple design choices, including the selection of distillation targets, teacher-student capacity alignment, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques to achieve reliable results.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.
