papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables efficient inference and reduced computational requirements across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a necessary and central component of any practical model compression strategy, supported by diverse methodologies, extensive empirical validation, and addressing both the strengths and limitations of the approach.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple mechanisms and approaches, ranging from soft-target matching to feature-level alignment, and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, making it an essential tool for practical model deployment.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while transferring learned knowledge. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation operates through teacher-student learning frameworks that transfer knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors. The technique addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Engineering-First Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a universal solution, knowledge distillation represents a context-dependent engineering practice that requires deliberate alignment of transfer mechanisms, teacher-student capacity matching, data availability strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques. This paper argues that when applied thoughtfully as a composable toolkit combining soft-target supervision, intermediate representation alignment, and task-specific design choices, knowledge distillation routinely enables practical deployments across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains while addressing real-world constraints in latency, memory, and computational cost.

papers_seen.author: Gregory
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. Treated as a composable core within a broader compression pipeline, KD supports multiple transfer mechanisms (soft targets, intermediate features, relational objectives, online/peer schemes, and data-aware variants) and complements pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Real-world success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity and deployment constraints, choosing appropriate data strategies, and diagnosing risks such as bias transfer or loss of rare behaviors. When designed with task awareness and combined with complementary methods, KD enables efficient, robust deployment across NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—such as softened logits, intermediate representations, and relational signals—and is typically integrated with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, and speech tasks, but practical success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, data choices, and explicit evaluation of robustness, privacy, and long-tail behavior. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, reliable distillation with limited or private data, and preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors under compression.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a compact, flexible, and empirically effective route to compress large neural models into deployable students. When treated as a design-first tool rather than a single loss term, KD can be combined with pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level objectives, data-efficient and data-free techniques, and architecture- or task-aware adjustments to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Adopting KD as the default strategy requires engineering practices that explicitly address teacher–student alignment, domain shift, rare-token behavior, and evaluation protocols, but doing so yields a practical, composable pipeline for converting research-scale models into production-ready systems.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. The approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains by transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student architectures. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, layer-wise supervision, and data-free synthesis approaches. When strategically combined with complementary techniques and careful architectural design, knowledge distillation provides robust solutions to real-world deployment challenges including latency reduction, memory constraints, and privacy preservation.

papers_seen.author: Glass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Composable, and Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a composable element in integrated compression pipelines, KD enables substantial reductions in inference latency, memory footprint, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. Realizing KD's benefits in production requires task-aware objectives, careful teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data approaches), and explicit attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task- and deployment-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or private data, KD yields substantial gains in size, latency, and efficiency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a one-size-fits-all solution: its success depends on careful selection of distilled signals, complementary structural compression techniques, and rigorous evaluation under domain shift, rare-event behavior, and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hines
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning internal features or relational signals, and are commonly composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data-free approaches). Empirically, KD routinely achieves favorable size–performance tradeoffs across vision and language tasks, but its effectiveness depends on careful teacher–student design, the choice and availability of distillation data, and explicit evaluation of robustness, privacy, and long-tail behaviors. Ongoing work focuses on data-constrained settings, robust transfer of internal behaviors, and integrating KD into deployment-aware compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation has evolved from a simple heuristic technique into a versatile, mature framework with diverse methodologies and broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning domains. Success with knowledge distillation depends on careful matching of compression strategies to task-specific constraints and deployment requirements rather than reliance on a single universal approach.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from complex teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in practical, real-world environments with limited computational resources. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains and application areas, making it essential for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique in deep learning that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach facilitates model compression without significant performance degradation, making it highly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning, with various methodological innovations improving its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Flexible Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables strong trade-offs between inference efficiency and predictive performance across domains such as NLP and vision. Real-world success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, combining KD with complementary compression methods, and using task- and data-aware strategies to preserve robustness and rare or structured knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Context-Aware Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, adaptable component of modern model-compression pipelines. KD provides a range of interchangeable signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational objectives, and synthetic-data schemes) that, when combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, enable deployment of efficient models across diverse tasks and resource regimes. Effective use of KD requires explicit choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student inductive biases, how to manage data and privacy constraints, and how to evaluate robustness and rare-case behavior. This position emphasizes KD’s practical versatility while acknowledging its context dependence and the open research needs needed to make distilled models reliably safe and fair in production.

papers_seen.author: Grimes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a central, composable component of broader model compression pipelines rather than a standalone solution. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, inference latency, memory constraints, and privacy preservation across diverse domains. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to task-specific design choices, integration with complementary compression techniques, and explicit evaluation of robustness and undesirable behavior transfer.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems in practically constrained environments. The approach encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from simple soft-target matching to sophisticated intermediate representation alignment, and when combined with complementary compression techniques, represents the core strategy for reliable and practical neural network deployment across multiple domains.

papers_seen.author: Acosta
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning and NLP systems on devices with strict latency, memory, and computational efficiency constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as the central strategy in any production-oriented compression pipeline, particularly when combined with complementary compression techniques and applied with careful attention to teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, and task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, distillation enables practitioners to reduce inference latency and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The approach spans diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains, making it essential for practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to lightweight student networks through various mechanisms, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and resource constraints. The field has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher strategies, data-aware techniques, and privacy-preserving methods across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or synthesized training signals. Across vision and language domains, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. Empirical practice treats KD as a composable element combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curricula, and data-synthesis strategies. Key practical considerations include choosing what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention), aligning teacher signals to student capacity, and handling limited or private data. Important open problems remain in robustness, fairness transfer, principled target selection, and automating task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Fischer
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and latency while preserving predictive performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching softened output distributions to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, attention transfer, multi-teacher fusion, data-centric strategies (including data-free and synthetic-data approaches), and integration with other compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. Practical success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, data availability, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods; remaining challenges include robust transfer of rare or structured knowledge, preserving fairness and adversarial robustness, and automating design choices for diverse deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models while preserving task performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, interpretability, and cross-device heterogeneity. Effective application requires choosing or designing KD variants that match the deployment constraint (e.g., layer matching for transformers, meta-learning teachers, data-free generation, or federated output sharing). When combined with complementary compression practices (progressive replacement, architectural search, or attention-based feature matching), KD routinely yields compact models suitable for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, significantly reducing computational requirements, inference latency, and memory consumption while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, with approaches ranging from output-level soft-target matching to feature-level and attention-based transfers. Practical success depends on careful design of distillation objectives, teacher-student alignment, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so compact systems can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature shows a wide family of methods — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational and task-specific mappings, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies such as augmentation, synthetic data, or pre-training compact architectures — that together enable strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical successes span vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, but open issues remain, including teacher–student mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, limited or absent training data, and principled design of what to transfer for particular student capacities. Practical deployments benefit from combining complementary techniques (representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, pre-training of small models, and continual or task-adaptive strategies) and from careful tuning of teacher construction, data, and transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from an ad-hoc trick into a versatile, broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models while preserving or transferring desirable behaviors. KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and it adapts across modalities and tasks when paired with task-aware objectives and complementary compression techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational tool in model-compression toolkits and outlines practical emphases—preserving internal representations, using feature- and attention-level supervision where appropriate, supporting data- and communication-constrained settings, and designing teacher-student couplings matched to the target task.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive, Composable Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) effectively compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD is broadly applicable across modalities and tasks, reduces inference cost and memory, and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques. However, its success depends on teacher–student alignment, available data, and targeted optimization; KD should therefore be treated as the default starting point for compression pipelines but applied with diagnostics, task-aware choices, and complementary methods to address robustness, privacy, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Treated as a composable core operation, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, and relational signals; it also complements pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Realizing KD's full value requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability (including low- or no-data regimes), objective design, and evaluation of robustness and fairness. When applied thoughtfully and combined with complementary techniques, KD enables efficient deployment of deep learning and NLP systems under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. When combined with careful design of student capacity, layer alignment, and complementary compression methods, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, available data, and how student and teacher internals align. Practical deployments benefit from treating KD as a multi-strategy engineering problem—selecting appropriate distillation targets, leveraging multi-teacher or data-free options when necessary, and addressing optimization gaps and low-frequency phenomena through task-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A flexible family of methods—including softened-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention imitation, multi-teacher and data-free variants—enables large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints, and KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Reyes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses logits-level (soft-target) matching, feature- and layer-wise mimicry, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware variants (including data-free and privacy-aware approaches). When treated as a configurable component within a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data augmentation—KD enables deployment of performant models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, language, graph, and multimodal settings. Practical success requires careful teacher–student alignment, chosen distillation targets, and evaluation for robustness and distributional changes.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Strategic Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate feature alignment, and self-distillation approaches. By addressing the critical challenge of deploying computationally intensive models on memory and latency-limited devices, knowledge distillation has become indispensable across diverse domains in deep learning and natural language processing, offering practical solutions for real-world applications where efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, achieving substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized tasks. Knowledge distillation should be understood as a flexible, composable toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all solution, requiring careful consideration of what knowledge to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Framework for Model Compression and Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. The method addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency reduction without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures, improves model robustness, and supports learning from ensembles, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lara
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade this has evolved from output logits matching to a toolkit that includes soft targets, intermediate representation and attention transfers, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data-centric strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving data), and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distillation routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs in vision and language tasks, but practical effectiveness depends on careful design of distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and evaluation under robustness and distribution-shift scenarios. Remaining challenges include principled selection of transfer targets, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, automated task-aware compression, and robust transfer of structured or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms (soft targets, feature imitation, contrastive alignment, multi-teacher pipelines, and data distillation) and is effective across domains including NLP, machine translation, recommendation, and graph and multimodal models. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture replacement), KD enables deployment on resource-constrained hardware while largely preserving performance. Success hinges on choices of distillation targets, teacher quality, data and augmentation strategies, and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the output of a larger, more capable teacher network. The method addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining performance quality. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, and information retrieval systems.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Multi-Strategy Approach for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single algorithmic trick but as an engineering paradigm that integrates teacher design, student capacity, data strategy, representation objectives, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware practices (privacy, federated protocols, pre-training of small architectures), KD routinely enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements while preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD has limits: teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity in federated settings, and fairness or distribution-shift failures demand careful, task-aware design and evaluation. The practical position advocated here is that KD should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines, with choice of techniques driven by operational constraints and empirical validation.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. These methods involve transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations in knowledge distillation across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and graph neural networks. The review highlights mechanisms that enable successful knowledge transfer, strategies for handling heterogeneous model architectures, data-free distillation approaches, and applications to federated learning and multi-modal learning systems.

By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory usage, and inference latency across diverse domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines rather than as a isolated algorithmic trick, though its effectiveness depends on careful task-aware design, thoughtful integration with complementary techniques, and consideration of important practical limitations.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted framework for compressing large neural networks into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, generative, and neural-architecture-search settings, methods vary from matching soft labels to aligning intermediate features, using attention-based layer projection, contrastive alignment, and optimization-aware divergences. Practical adaptations address data availability, privacy, and efficiency constraints, while empirical and theoretical analyses reveal optimization limits, dataset and heterogeneity sensitivities, and opportunities from meta-learning teachers and task-specific design. Despite broad success, key open problems remain in reliably preserving teacher knowledge, designing data- and privacy-aware protocols, and tailoring distillation to domain-specific structures.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher model, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing performance. This approach has become increasingly important across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, offering significant speedup and reduced computational requirements while maintaining competitive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD has matured into a toolkit that includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature transfer, multi-teacher schedules, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and domain-specific variants. As a result, KD should be treated as a central element of any production-oriented compression pipeline—but it must be applied with attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, task requirements, and complementary compression methods to achieve reliable, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mccarty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical default for compressing large models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. As a flexible, composable toolkit, KD can transfer output behavior, internal representations, and relational structure; it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation; and it supports data-aware strategies for privacy- or data-constrained settings. Realizing its benefits requires deliberate choices about distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and handling of domain shift or teacher errors, but when applied as an engineering-first, context-sensitive framework KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs for production deployments.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. The field has evolved from simple output logit matching to a diverse toolkit encompassing intermediate-representation alignment, attention transfer, multi-teacher approaches, and data-free methods. Practical success depends on careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, selection of what knowledge to transfer, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques. Important open challenges remain around robustness to distribution shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and operating without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Strategy for Compressing Deep and Pre-trained NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. Across NLP and related vision and multimodal tasks, KD enables substantial inference speedups, can be combined with complementary compression methods, and benefits from targeted algorithmic improvements — at the data, model, and teacher-selection levels — to close the gap to teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. I argue that KD should be a core component of real-world model-compression toolkits, used together with techniques such as careful pretraining of compact architectures, data augmentation, feature-level matching, and teacher-ensemble strategies to maximize accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique in deep learning that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach facilitates model compression without significant performance degradation, making it highly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning, with various methodological innovations improving its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Lindsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as the primary and most practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the default compression strategy when properly combined with complementary techniques and carefully designed to address real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Buchanan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal information. KD comprises a family of methods—matching softened outputs, imitating internal representations, leveraging multiple teachers, and synthesizing data when originals are unavailable—and is widely used to reduce inference latency, memory footprint, and energy use so that state-of-the-art models can be deployed in constrained settings. Practical success depends on aligning signals to student capacity, handling data availability and distribution shifts, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (e.g., pruning, quantization). Important open problems include robust data-free distillation, principled teacher design, heterogeneity in federated settings, and preserving fairness and robustness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Luna
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models through diverse mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and attention-based transfers, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, including what knowledge is transferred, teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques. When treated as a composable core component of broader compression pipelines and adapted to task-specific constraints, knowledge distillation represents an essential engineering paradigm for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning models into practical deployment across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to students. When treated as a composable, task-aware toolkit—combined with signal selection, architecture alignment, and complementary compression methods—KD enables efficient deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a silver bullet: careful design, domain-aware adaptation, and rigorous evaluation are required to avoid failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch, distributional shift, and unintended transfer of biases.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning internal representations, adversarial/generative teacher-student games, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or augmentation-driven pipelines. Distillation is widely used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on constrained hardware, and adapt models when training data is limited or sensitive. Practical deployments require careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare data and augmentations, and whether to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. Open problems include data-free distillation, principled teacher design for student friendliness, robust multi-teacher aggregation, and aligning representations across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Gallegos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Core Mechanisms and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning and natural language processing systems across diverse applications. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and strategies, and when properly designed and combined with other compression techniques, provides substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency without significant accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The approach spans matching softened logits, mimicking intermediate features, adversarial and generative teacher-student games, and data- or architecture-aware pipelines. Empirical work shows distillation preserves much teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability, and the design of transfer signals. Ongoing directions include theory for when distillation improves generalization, task- and modality-specific objectives (including generation and multimodal transfer), and practical strategies for data-free or privacy-preserving compression.

papers_seen.author: Washington
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression approaches enable practical deployment of large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from high-capacity teachers into smaller students. A rich set of distillation mechanisms—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise imitation, relational or task-aware filtering, and many-to-many layer mapping—have been developed and combined with data-side strategies and architectural design. Practical success depends on aligning objectives to student capacity and task constraints; open problems include teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity and privacy, representational alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and principled guarantees for robustness and fairness.
