papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practically indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression techniques, represents a comprehensive toolkit that addresses critical real-world deployment challenges while remaining flexible enough to adapt to varying task requirements, data availability, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD has matured into a flexible family of techniques—logit or soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention transfer, multi-teacher strategies, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and other modalities, but practical success depends on student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and careful engineering of objectives and schedules.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for compressing large models, transferring knowledge across architectures, enabling private or federated workflows, and improving efficiency for deployment in resource-constrained settings. While KD often yields substantial practical gains—reducing model size and inference cost with limited loss in performance—it has important theoretical and empirical limitations related to optimization, data dependence, model and domain heterogeneity, and teacher–student mismatch. A pragmatic stance recognizes KD as a versatile toolset whose effectiveness depends on how it is applied: the choice of distilled targets (logits, features, or relations), the availability or synthesis of data, the use of multiple teachers or staged procedures, and awareness of when distillation can harm or help generalization. This paper argues that KD should be used as part of a broader compression and adaptation strategy guided by empirical diagnostics and appropriate extensions (multi-teacher, zero-shot/data-free, federated/distilled protocols, or self-supervised distillation) rather than as an off-the-shelf cure-all.

This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely a complementary technique but a central and essential strategy that enables practical deployment across diverse applications and domains.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. Research expands the basic soft-target paradigm into methods that align intermediate representations, use multi-teacher or online protocols, and operate under constrained data regimes (including data-free and adversarial sample generation). Distillation is widely applied in NLP (including compressed pretrained language models and domain-adaptive students), vision, multimodal systems, and large-scale industrial training pipelines. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data availability and domain shift, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques while accounting for robustness and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster models by transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, or relational structure. In deep learning and NLP, KD is used both to reduce inference cost and to adapt large pretrained models to new domains or resource-constrained settings. Practical KD pipelines balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity, employ selective or curriculum-driven training data, and can combine with quantization or low-precision methods to meet latency and memory constraints. While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on data complexity, teacher quality, and how teacher knowledge is exposed to the student; these dependencies produce both opportunities (e.g., domain-specific distilled models) and risks (e.g., propagation of teacher errors). Current work advances theoretical understanding, proposes methods for student- and task-aware teacher design, and extends KD to robustness, large-scale distributed training, and low-precision deployment.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single algorithmic trick but as an engineering paradigm that integrates teacher design, student capacity, data strategy, representation objectives, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware practices (privacy, federated protocols, pre-training of small architectures), KD routinely enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements while preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD has limits: teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity in federated settings, and fairness or distribution-shift failures demand careful, task-aware design and evaluation. The practical position advocated here is that KD should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines, with choice of techniques driven by operational constraints and empirical validation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses diverse mechanisms — soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention/relational matching, progressive replacement, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free or privacy-aware variants — and is most effective when integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search) and when teacher–student design, data strategies, and evaluation criteria are chosen to match deployment requirements. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, available (or synthesized) distillation data, and active monitoring for transferred failures. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a composable, diagnostic-driven component of model-compression toolkits rather than a single turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from one or more teacher models. KD has evolved into a flexible framework that includes soft-target matching, feature and layer imitation, multi-teacher strategies, data-free approaches, and integration with architecture search and other compression techniques. Across domains—especially natural language processing and computer vision—careful matching of distillation signals, data strategies, and student capacity yields practical, deployable models that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and energy consumption. Remaining challenges include handling absent or private data, aligning inductive biases between teacher and student, preserving robustness and fairness, and automating task-aware compression decisions.

papers_seen.author: Simpson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the primary default strategy for model compression across deep learning and natural language processing applications. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through diverse mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment in latency-, memory-, and energy-constrained environments. While its effectiveness depends on careful design choices and complementary compression techniques, the evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation consistently delivers substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Pragmatic Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, this approach enables practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. However, while knowledge distillation is highly effective in many scenarios, its success is not universal and depends critically on careful design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between training conditions and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models through various mechanisms, enabling significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. The field encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-representation alignment, and has demonstrated broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, making it an essential tool for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Default Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The technique encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and can be strategically combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, signal selection, data availability, and task-specific adaptation. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the default starting point for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP systems, provided it is paired with principled design workflows and comprehensive evaluation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Multifaceted, and Engineering-Driven for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Effective KD requires more than a single loss term: it is an engineering-driven, multi-strategy process involving teacher construction, what signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), data and augmentation choices, and careful alignment of teacher and student capacity. When integrated with complementary compression methods and diagnostic practices, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models in latency-, memory-, and energy-constrained environments, though its success depends on thoughtful design to avoid transferring teacher errors or degrading rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental training paradigm in which a large, well-trained teacher model transfers learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as essential for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, serving as a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity neural networks into smaller, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to student models. KD encompasses a family of techniques — including soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, ensemble and online strategies, and data-aware variants — and is widely used to reduce inference latency, memory, and computational cost while preserving task performance. Its practical success depends on careful choices about distilled targets, teacher–student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; KD is powerful and broadly applicable but not a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Essential for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models. This approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation operates through multiple complementary mechanisms—including soft-target matching, intermediate feature alignment, and data-centric strategies—and addresses critical real-world challenges such as computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, and privacy preservation. While KD effectiveness depends on careful design of teacher-student pairs, choice of distillation objectives, and data availability, extensive empirical evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation, when properly integrated into hybrid compression pipelines, represents the most versatile and practical approach to achieving efficient neural networks across diverse applications.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, and task-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple mechanisms, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains under stringent computational, memory, and latency constraints. The technique encompasses various complementary methodologies and requires careful attention to design choices, teacher-student alignment, and domain-specific adaptation to achieve optimal compression and performance tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning and NLP models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models. The method has been successfully applied across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks like object detection and speech recognition, demonstrating consistent improvements in model efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multipurpose Tool for Model Compression and Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a principled, adaptable framework that can both reduce model size and provide transfer, robustness, and deployment advantages when combined with complementary techniques. A practical KD-centered strategy emphasizes transferring intermediate representations in addition to logits, leveraging multiple and domain-aware teachers, accommodating imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and adapting to constraints such as privacy or federated settings. When KD is used alongside pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design, it enables compact models that approach the performance of much larger teachers while meeting latency, memory, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements while preserving much of the teacher's performance. The approach encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and can be combined with other compression strategies, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency and practical deployment across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Evidence, Design Principles, and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable component of a compression pipeline—selecting what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which complementary techniques to apply—KD routinely achieves favorable accuracy/efficiency tradeoffs across NLP, vision, and generative tasks. However, realizing reliable production outcomes requires task-aware choices, careful handling of teacher–student mismatch, and evaluation for robustness and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behaviors and internal structure. Across vision, language, graph, and specialized domains, KD methods include softened-output matching, intermediate-feature imitation, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free variants. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and when distillation objectives are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. Important open problems remain in principled teacher–student design, robustness under distribution shift, privacy and data-free distillation, and reliable transfer of rare or structured knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple output-level matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies and applications across deep learning and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals from teachers. KD spans soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, and progressive or online protocols. When combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD produces strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision, speech, and language tasks. Its practical success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, data strategy (including use or synthesis of distilled examples), and task-aware evaluation; failure modes include optimization difficulty, teacher-induced errors on rare tokens, and distribution-shift sensitivity. This synthesis summarizes established mechanisms, common applications and failure modes, and practical design guidelines drawn from recent empirical and analytical work.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behaviors and internal structure. Across modalities, KD includes multiple mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, adversarial and regularized objectives, and multi-teacher or curriculum schemes—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful, task-aware design. Important open issues remain around robustness under distribution shift, principled teacher–student design, data-constrained or data-free settings, and preserving rare or structured knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across vision and language tasks, KD methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning internal representations and attention, and are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Practical deployment depends on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, what data to use (including synthetic or task-adaptive data), and how to evaluate robustness and rare-behavior preservation. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical combinations with complementary compression methods, task-aware adaptations, and recurring engineering and research challenges for applying distillation in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems across diverse domains under stringent latency, memory, and computational constraints. The field encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and methodologies, ranging from simple soft-target matching to sophisticated intermediate representation alignment and task-aware compression strategies. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it an indispensable method for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Baird
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A variety of distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and using synthesized or adversarially generated supervision—enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often maintaining much of the teacher’s performance. Practical deployment of KD is most effective when it is treated as a composable component of broader compression pipelines that also include pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Key operational factors that determine success include teacher–student capacity alignment, availability and choice of data for distillation, and targeted optimization of distilled signals; important open challenges are robustness under domain shift, privacy- or data-constrained distillation, and principled selection of distilled targets for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and powerful approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining or improving performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models through various mechanisms, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and resource constraints. Knowledge distillation is increasingly recognized as an essential strategy across computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized domains, serving not only compression but also regularization, privacy preservation, and knowledge transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses diverse strategies spanning output-level supervision, intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware adaptations, with successful applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This synthesis examines core mechanisms, common variants, practical implementation strategies, and key considerations for achieving effective model compression.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency, recent research reveals important limitations and nuances in how knowledge transfer occurs, and highlights the importance of careful design choices and methodical application rather than treating distillation as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Composable, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. KD techniques—ranging from softened output matching to intermediate-representation and relational transfers—regularly yield large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, the value of KD depends on careful alignment of teacher signals with student capacity, appropriate handling of data regimes and domain shift, and integration with complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a central but context-aware component of compression pipelines yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Converging Strategies for Practical Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing classifiers into a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that enables deployment of large models in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings. Advances span architectural strategies (progressive module replacement and feature mimicking), data-centric solutions (data-free and augmented distillation), teacher selection (ensembles and meta-learned teachers), and objectives that transfer robustness as well as accuracy. When combined thoughtfully — e.g., targeted feature-level objectives, careful data-generation or augmentation, and teacher optimization — KD enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. This article argues that best practice is not a single KD recipe but an integrated approach that matches the distillation technique to operational constraints (data availability, privacy, robustness requirements, and target hardware).

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Pragmatic and Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving competitive performance. Rather than a single recipe, knowledge distillation represents a flexible toolkit of complementary methods—including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware strategies—that enable practitioners to deploy state-of-the-art models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of data availability and teacher-student design, knowledge distillation consistently achieves substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while maintaining much of the original teacher performance, making it indispensable for production deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically supported route to compress large neural models into deployable, efficient students. As a composable framework rather than a single algorithm, KD can be adapted to task constraints, combined with complementary compression methods, and tuned via data- and architecture-aware design choices to yield robust, high-performing models suitable for resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models in deep learning and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—via softened outputs, layer-wise feature targets, attention maps, or ensembles—KD enables strong size/performance trade-offs and supports many deployment settings (on-device, low-latency, privacy-constrained). Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the default, composable core of compression pipelines while acknowledging and addressing its practical limitations through principled engineering and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing intermediate-feature alignment, attention-based transfer, multi-teacher strategies, and data-aware adaptations, though practical success depends critically on careful design choices and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the core, practical default for compressing high-capacity neural models into deployable students for deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible supervision beyond hard labels, supports many transfer signals (logits, features, relational patterns), and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, realizing KD’s potential requires explicit attention to what is transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data regimes, and robustness and fairness risks. When applied as a composable component of a broader compression pipeline and tailored to task and deployment constraints, KD reliably produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling efficient deployment across computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal domains. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching into a sophisticated toolkit that can be combined with complementary compression strategies such as pruning and quantization. However, practical success depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, data availability, and handling of potential failure modes including bias transfer and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and representational signals. In practice KD encompasses a family of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature mimicry, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and task-aware or data-free variants—that are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher’s performance, but its success depends on careful matching of signals to student capacity, data availability, and robustness goals. Key limitations include teacher–student mismatch, sensitivity to data heterogeneity and distribution shift, and potential transfer of undesirable biases; addressing these requires task-aware pipelines, representation-level transfer, and rigorous evaluation under deployment stresses.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for producing compact models that enable deployment of modern deep learning and NLP systems under resource constraints. When treated as a composable core operation in a broader compression pipeline—and applied with task-aware choices about teacher signal, student capacity, data strategy, and evaluation—KD yields strong size/performance trade-offs. However, KD is not a drop-in cure: careful diagnostics, complementary compression techniques, and attention to teacher–student mismatch, robustness, and data limitations are required to realize reliable production outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible framework for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or contrastive embeddings, and they are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques. Across modalities and tasks, KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs, though success depends on choices of distillation targets, teacher quality, student capacity, and data strategies. Ongoing directions emphasize data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, preserving robustness and internal representations, and adapting distillation to task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mccarty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical default for compressing large models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. As a flexible, composable toolkit, KD can transfer output behavior, internal representations, and relational structure; it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation; and it supports data-aware strategies for privacy- or data-constrained settings. Realizing its benefits requires deliberate choices about distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and handling of domain shift or teacher errors, but when applied as an engineering-first, context-sensitive framework KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs for production deployments.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthetic signals. A diverse set of distillation mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, feature and layer alignment, relational and attention-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or adversarial sample generation—enable substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on thoughtful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity relationships, available data, and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Remaining challenges include robustness under domain shift, preserving rare-case behavior, privacy-preserving distillation without original data, and principled selection of student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized training signals. KD reduces model size, inference latency, memory footprint, and energy consumption while retaining much of teacher performance across domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graphs, and generative modelling. Practical success depends on choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and architecture, handling limited or private data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is highly effective in many deployment scenarios but has empirical and theoretical limits that require task-aware design, careful evaluation, and integration into broader compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compress large models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Empirical and methodological advances show KD succeeds when (1) the teacher signals are adapted to student capacity, (2) internal representations and attention patterns are aligned when architectures differ, and (3) distillation is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, low-precision, pretraining) and task-aware training regimes. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: carefully chosen losses, multi-source reliability estimation, feature-level objectives, and integration with pretraining or hardware-aware compression yield the best trade-offs between model size, speed, and accuracy across vision, language, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential, Practical, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically effective technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. KD methods—ranging from logit-level supervision and feature/attention imitation to ensemble, multi-teacher, and data-free variants—have enabled real-world gains in latency, memory, and cross-device applicability across NLP, vision, speech, and graph tasks. At the same time, KD’s benefits depend on careful design choices (what to transfer, how to generate or select data, and how to match teacher and student capacity), and there are empirical and theoretical limitations that counsel a measured, diagnostic-driven application rather than blind deployment. This paper argues that KD is an essential component of modern model-compression toolkits but not a panacea: its success requires method selection, data or metadata strategies, and complementary techniques to manage trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reassessing Knowledge Distillation: Regularization, Teacher Quality, and Task-Driven Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile tool for compressing models and transferring capabilities from large teachers to smaller students across vision, graph, 3D, and NLP tasks. Its effectiveness arises not only from transmitting teacher class similarities but also from the regularizing properties of soft targets and from mimicking intermediate representations. Recent advances demonstrate that KD can be applied without direct access to a strong pretrained teacher or original training data, and that task-specific distillation objectives (contrastive, adversarial, feature-level) often outperform naive logit matching. At the same time, optimization barriers, teacher errors, and domain shifts can limit or bias distilled students, so practitioners should choose distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings that align with the target task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A broad family of KD techniques has been developed — including soft-target (logits) matching, intermediate representation and attention mimicry, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free variants — and KD is routinely combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. In practice, KD enables deployment of effective models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across NLP and other domains, but its success depends on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and quality, and evaluation for robustness and distributional shift. Ongoing challenges include automating design choices, preserving robustness and fairness, handling private or absent data, and diagnosing teacher-student mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Mack
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default: A Task-Aware, Composable Approach for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective method for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques, KD provides a practical route to reduce latency, memory, and compute while largely preserving task performance. However, its benefits depend on careful teacher–student design, the choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be the default starting point for model compression in deep learning and NLP, applied deliberately and adapted to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, flexible approach for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, efficient students that can meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and privacy. Over the past decade KD has diversified from softened-logit matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention transfer, adversarial and data-augmentation-driven strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble compression methods, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical work demonstrates that, when carefully engineered with attention to teacher quality, student capacity alignment, and appropriate data regimes, distillation routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs across vision and language tasks, while remaining sensitive to distributional shift, transferred failures, and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical default within model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP because it provides a flexible, widely applicable way to transfer behavior from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. When used as a composable toolkit—combining output-level supervision, representation imitation, curriculum and multi-teacher strategies, and complementary compression methods—KD yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained deployments. Success requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and robustness evaluation; adopting KD as the default therefore implies system-level practices that validate transferred behavior under distribution shift and integrate other compression techniques when appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. Knowledge distillation operates through the transfer of soft targets and intermediate representations from teacher to student networks, providing implicit regularization and accelerating convergence. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, information retrieval, and speech processing, offering substantial reductions in model size and computational cost with minimal performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Advancing Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a compact student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. While the foundational concept has been widely applied across computer vision, recommender systems, and natural language processing, recent advances have introduced sophisticated variations and domain-specific adaptations. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective distillation approaches, cross-modal knowledge transfer, adversarial learning frameworks, and specialized applications to transformer-based architectures and sequential tasks.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted approach to compress high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Empirical results show KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance across vision, speech, and language tasks and supports many variants (e.g., feature matching, ensemble transfer, self-distillation, and data-free strategies). At the same time, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, teacher–student mismatch, and data availability introduce limits that require methodical choices (what to transfer, how to train, and when to synthesize or curate data). Careful design—combining representation-level objectives, architecture-aware mapping, multi-teacher or adversarial schemes, and federated or zero-shot adaptations—yields the best practical trade-offs for accuracy, cost, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges such as latency reduction, memory efficiency, energy consumption, and privacy concerns. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, when thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and adapted to task-specific constraints, represents an essential and practical framework for enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from an ad-hoc trick into a versatile, broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models while preserving or transferring desirable behaviors. KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and it adapts across modalities and tasks when paired with task-aware objectives and complementary compression techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational tool in model-compression toolkits and outlines practical emphases—preserving internal representations, using feature- and attention-level supervision where appropriate, supporting data- and communication-constrained settings, and designing teacher-student couplings matched to the target task.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a foundational, composable technique for compressing deep and NLP models: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and representations from high-capacity teachers into smaller students, and when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis or adversarial training) it enables practical deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to handle data and teacher quality, and how to integrate KD into an end-to-end compression pipeline; when used with these considerations it yields compact, robust models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, size, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.
