papers_seen.author: Fields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while preserving competitive performance. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from soft-target matching and intermediate representation alignment to multi-teacher ensembles and self-distillation. When combined with complementary compression techniques and applied with careful consideration of task-specific constraints, KD addresses critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art models across vision, language, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a core, composable component of modern compression pipelines that should be treated as an essential engineering paradigm for practical deep learning deployment. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks through multiple complementary mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware procedures (including data-free and synthetic-data approaches). In practice KD is typically combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data or pretraining strategies to produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Success depends on design choices about what signals to transfer, how to align representations across capacity-mismatched networks, and how to handle limited or private data; remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and automating task-adaptive distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Beltran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context-Dependent Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a central, adaptable component of production-ready compression pipelines. When applied with task- and capacity-aware design, paired with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis), and evaluated for robustness, fairness, and privacy, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving behavior critical for real-world deep learning and NLP systems. Practical success requires explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to manage data—choices that make KD a context-dependent tool rather than a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Multi-Objective View of Knowledge Distillation for Robust, Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical route to compress large neural models for deployment, but treating distillation as merely matching teacher output probabilities limits what can be transferred and how reliably the student will generalize. This paper argues that effective distillation should combine representation-level transfer, channel- and feature-aware objectives, confidence-weighted multi-teacher signals, domain adaptation, and training-time efficiency techniques, while explicitly attending to optimization gaps and fairness concerns. We synthesize evidence across methods and propose a prioritized, pragmatic pipeline for producing compact models that better retain teacher knowledge, scale in production, and reduce unintended harms.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Cordova
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through various complementary mechanisms, enabling efficient deployment across diverse domains. KD encompasses multiple methodologies and strategies that address critical practical challenges in real-world deployment scenarios, including computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, and privacy preservation.

papers_seen.author: Rose
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default and Composable Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical default for model compression in deep learning and NLP because it provides a flexible, empirically validated way to transfer task-relevant behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD functions best as a composable core: it is effective on its own and most powerful when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, or data synthesis). However, realizing KD's potential requires task- and deployment-aware choices about signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data regimes, and explicit evaluation of robustness and undesirable behavior transfer.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. Over the past decade KD evolved from matching soft logits into a broad set of techniques—feature-level and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, curriculum and architecture-aware strategies—that collectively enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation objectives, data regimes, and student architectures to deployment constraints; open issues include teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Mendez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By systematically transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a mature, composable framework that is essential for modern neural network deployment, though its effectiveness depends critically on careful architectural design, appropriate data strategies, and integration with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in modern deep learning deployment and has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a central tool in modern machine learning, combining algorithmic innovations with thoughtful design choices to achieve reliable, production-ready compression results.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and latency while retaining task performance. Over the past decade KD has moved beyond simple soft-target matching to a composable toolkit that includes feature- and layer-wise alignment, relational and attention-based objectives, multi-teacher and teacher-free setups, and data-aware or data-free procedures. Practical deployment couples KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful attention to teacher–student design, data strategies, and robustness under distribution shift. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, fairness and privacy transfer, and automating teacher–student optimization.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential and Context-Dependent Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while addressing critical deployment challenges. However, realizing the full potential of knowledge distillation requires careful attention to teacher-student alignment, selection of appropriate transfer mechanisms, data availability strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques. This paper argues that while knowledge distillation should serve as a core component of modern compression pipelines, its success depends on principled, context-dependent design choices rather than universal application.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Bridging Performance and Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. The technique applies across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation, demonstrating its versatility as a general-purpose compression method. By training smaller student models to mimic larger teacher models, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost without substantial accuracy degradation, making it essential for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Contextual and Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a universal solution, knowledge distillation is most effective when treated as a flexible, composable element of a broader compression strategy that accounts for task-specific requirements, data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, and deployment constraints. This position synthesizes evidence across deep learning and NLP domains to argue that successful knowledge distillation requires careful orchestration of what knowledge is transferred, how it is transferred, and the data and architectural decisions that support the distillation process.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational and Practical Path to Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary methods—hardware-aware pruning, data augmentation, many-to-many layer alignment, and data-free distillation—KD enables practical deployment across modalities and devices. Responsible application requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and bias transfer, and benefits from integrating KD into broader compression toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. Through various mechanisms and strategic design choices, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Rodgers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies and requires careful attention to design choices, teacher-student alignment, and domain-specific adaptation to achieve optimal compression and performance trade-offs. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms, methodological variations, practical strategies, empirical outcomes, and remaining challenges in knowledge distillation and model compression across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. This approach addresses fundamental practical challenges such as inference latency, memory consumption, and computational requirements without significant accuracy loss. When combined with complementary compression strategies and applied thoughtfully to specific task requirements, knowledge distillation becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art models into real-world systems operating under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD unifies multiple transfer mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation imitation, attention or projector-based mapping, multi-teacher fusion, curriculum-driven training, and data-free or federated distillation—making it applicable across vision, language, retrieval, and on-device scenarios. When combined with domain adaptation and careful teacher–student alignment, KD enables substantial reductions in model size, latency, and computational cost while preserving task performance, though success depends on method selection, data availability, and optimization choices.

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential and Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while retaining much of the teacher's performance. This approach transfers knowledge through multiple mechanisms—from soft-target matching to feature alignment and attention transfer—and has been successfully applied across computer vision, natural language processing, speech, and multimodal systems. When thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and adapted to specific task and deployment constraints, knowledge distillation provides reliable solutions for enabling efficient inference in resource-constrained environments. However, realizing its full potential requires careful attention to teacher-student design choices, data strategies, and comprehensive evaluation across robustness and edge-case behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving predictive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, with diverse approaches adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Neural Network Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models across deep learning and natural language processing. While distillation provides flexible mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher to student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency, its effectiveness is highly context-dependent. Successful deployment requires careful attention to teacher-student capacity alignment, deliberate selection of distillation signals, integration with complementary compression methods, and explicit evaluation of potential failure modes including robustness, fairness, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through diverse mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables efficient inference and reduced computational requirements across domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential component of modern model compression strategies, supported by extensive empirical validation across diverse methodologies and applications, while acknowledging the challenges and design considerations necessary for successful implementation.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental and Composable Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a primary, default tool for model compression across deep learning and NLP domains when applied thoughtfully as part of an integrated compression pipeline that addresses teacher-student alignment, data availability, robustness concerns, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Berg
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When treated as a composable, task-aware engineering toolkit—transferring soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals, or synthetic training examples—KD yields favorable size/performance tradeoffs and integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: success requires careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation signals and data strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and transferred undesirable behaviors. Practitioners should adopt KD as a first-line compression method while designing pipelines and evaluations that address its known limitations.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals, multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies) and is effective across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, its success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, data availability and handling, choice of distilled targets, and integration with complementary compression techniques. Treated as a composable operation within broader compression pipelines and executed with task-aware diagnostics, KD enables realistic deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When treated as a composable, task-aware engineering toolkit—transferring soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals, or synthetic training examples—KD yields favorable size/performance tradeoffs and integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: success requires careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation signals and data strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, privacy, and transferred undesirable behaviors. Practitioners should adopt KD as a first-line compression method while designing pipelines and evaluations that address its known limitations.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used family of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features, using ensembles or multiple teachers, online and adversarial schemes, and synthesizing or curating distillation data; when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) they enable practical deployment under latency, memory, and device constraints. Despite broad empirical success, important open problems remain around data availability and privacy, teacher–student design and capacity mismatch, robustness and fairness under compression, and domain- or task-specific phenomena such as low-frequency token behavior in NLP.

papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental training paradigm in which a large, well-trained teacher model transfers learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as essential for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, serving as a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Practical Paths and Limits for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving performance. KD has evolved from simple logit matching to diverse strategies that address data availability, task specificity, representation-level transfer, and architectural mismatches. However, fundamental limits—especially under heterogeneous data or federated settings—and practical challenges such as selecting useful teacher signal and coping with student capacity remain. A pragmatic approach combines data-aware or data-free sample generation, representation- and layer-level objectives, and task-aware filtering to maximize transfer while respecting privacy, compute, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. papers_seen.author: Anderson

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. However, its effectiveness depends strongly on data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, domain and task specifics, and system constraints; thus KD should be applied as a composable element of a compression strategy rather than as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and representational signals. In practice KD encompasses a family of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature mimicry, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and task-aware or data-free variants—that are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher’s performance, but its success depends on careful matching of signals to student capacity, data availability, and robustness goals. Key limitations include teacher–student mismatch, sensitivity to data heterogeneity and distribution shift, and potential transfer of undesirable biases; addressing these requires task-aware pipelines, representation-level transfer, and rigorous evaluation under deployment stresses.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods and Practice in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across deep learning and NLP, KD techniques range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations and relational structures, and they are routinely combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search, etc.) to meet practical constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling large reductions in model size and inference cost, but success depends on choices about teacher design, student capacity, the distillation objective, and data availability. Extensions such as federated and data-free distillation broaden applicability to privacy-sensitive and low-data settings; task-aware and layer-wise adaptations help align what is transferred to student capacity and task needs. Remaining challenges include representation alignment, optimization gaps between teachers and students, and principled guarantees for fairness and generalization, pointing toward composable, task-adaptive KD systems for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, composable approach for converting large teacher models into smaller student models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. The distillation toolkit includes soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online protocols, curriculum and data-aware strategies, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants. Best results typically come from combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and from aligning the distillation signal to student capacity and deployment constraints. Remaining gaps include robust transfer under distribution shift, reliable preservation of rare or structured behaviors, automated task-adaptive selection of objectives and architectures, and principled, privacy-aware workflows for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Morgan

The technique addresses critical challenges of inference latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, while supporting various practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity.

papers_seen.author: Durham

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. However, successful knowledge distillation requires careful attention to task-specific design choices, teacher-student alignment, and complementary compression techniques rather than serving as a universal one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Design Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven, versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD supports multiple transfer mechanisms (soft targets, representation alignment, relational and layer-wise objectives) and integrates well with complementary compression steps, enabling substantial reductions in inference latency and footprint for NLP and other domains. However, realizing these gains reliably requires careful choices about distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, handling scarce or private data, multi-teacher coordination, and robustness under distribution shift. When applied with task-aware design and complementary methods, KD should be treated as the practical default for model compression, not as a black-box panacea.

papers_seen.author: Morse
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate information. KD operates with multiple signal types (soft logits, feature- and attention-level targets, relational or contrastive objectives) and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Empirical work across vision, language, and graph domains shows KD can substantially reduce size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and explicit handling of robustness, rare or safety-critical behaviors, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Path to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Knowledge distillation has evolved from simple output-level matching to diverse methodologies encompassing feature-level mimicking, attention transfer, layer alignment, and task-adaptive schemes. The technique has demonstrated broad applicability across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making it an essential tool for modern machine learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Central Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible, composable framework that transfers logits, intermediate representations, or synthesized signals from high-capacity teachers to compact students. In production settings KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs when combined with complementary techniques (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture search, privacy-aware protocols) and when student objectives are adapted to capacity and deployment constraints. However, care is required to avoid transferring undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, overconfidence) and to address optimization gaps on low-frequency phenomena and under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: French
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile pathway to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameters, memory, and latency and has been validated across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. Effective distillation requires matching the distilled signal to the student capacity and data setting, and often works best when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design choices. When adapted to context (multi-teacher ensembles, limited data, or privacy constraints), distillation enables production-ready models that meet real-world resource and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Composable Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a composable toolkit—transferring logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals and combined with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs across modalities. At the same time, KD is not a silver bullet: success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, the data used for transfer, and explicit handling of robustness, rare behaviors, and privacy. This paper argues that KD should be the practical default for model compression in deep learning and NLP when applied with task-aware engineering and safeguards against known limitations.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, this approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and natural language processing systems in resource-limited environments. The method encompasses diverse strategies and mechanisms, addresses critical real-world challenges including computational efficiency and latency reduction, and has demonstrated broad applicability across multiple domains. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful design choices tailored to specific deployment constraints, it represents an essential strategy for practical neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Comprehensive Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices and accelerates inference times for real-world applications. Through teacher-student learning frameworks, knowledge distillation transfers learned representations from complex models to compact ones, addressing the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Limited Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. However, its practical success hinges on task-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods; it is a powerful tool but not a universal solution. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational and composable component of compression pipelines, paired with principled choices about targets, architectures, and training regimes to maximize utility while acknowledging optimization and data-driven limits.

papers_seen.author: Kerr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring learned behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under computation, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. KD includes matching teacher soft targets (logits), aligning intermediate representations or attention, staged or multi-teacher pipelines, and variants for data-free, online, and federated settings. Empirical work across vision, language, and other modalities shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling substantial resource savings, but success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Ongoing challenges include optimization gaps, teacher–student mismatch, fairness and robustness tradeoffs, and limitations under heterogeneous or private data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Composable Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When treated as a composable element within a broader compression pipeline, KD interoperates with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies to meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and privacy. However, its success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, and data availability; thus KD should be adopted as a foundational default with explicit caveats and evaluation protocols rather than as a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Dependent Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. However, realizing the full potential of knowledge distillation requires careful attention to multiple design factors including teacher-student alignment, selection of appropriate transfer mechanisms, data availability strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from teacher models. This approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, providing solutions to critical challenges of inference latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, and Context-Sensitive Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a practical, composable toolkit for compressing models for real deployments. Different distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational objectives, adversarial losses) and operational modalities (multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, task-aware scheduling) suit different domains and constraints. Realizing KD’s benefits requires matching what is distilled to student capacity and task demands, addressing data scarcity and distribution shift, and combining distillation with architectural and data strategies to preserve robustness and fairness while meeting latency and memory targets.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models across deep learning and natural language processing applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a central, practical toolkit for model compression—not as a single recipe, but as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to diverse deployment constraints and task requirements. By systematically reviewing the mechanisms, applications, and design principles of knowledge distillation, we demonstrate that thoughtfully applied distillation enables substantial reductions in computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency while preserving much of the original teacher performance.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains. This approach addresses critical challenges in reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency, making it an indispensable tool for modern machine learning deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that compact systems can approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a composable toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free distillation). Across vision and language tasks, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation design is adapted to task- and data-specific constraints. Remaining practical challenges include principled teacher selection, handling limited or private data, mitigating transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, overconfidence), and understanding when and why distillation improves generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to resource-constrained students, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. By addressing critical constraints of latency, memory efficiency, and computational cost, knowledge distillation has become essential for making sophisticated deep learning models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient deployment of neural networks. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring task-relevant information through soft targets, intermediate feature signals, or other auxiliary objectives. KD enables deployment of performant models under constraints of latency, memory, and privacy, and it forms a flexible engineering toolkit that can be combined with pretraining, multi-teacher fusion, domain adaptation, and robustness-oriented training. Practical success depends on choosing what to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize distillation data, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to evaluate students under the target deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Watson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as the fundamental and most practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. This position argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the central compression strategy in modern deep learning when combined with complementary techniques and carefully designed to address real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal settings. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention patterns, and operating in data-limited, privacy-sensitive, or federated scenarios. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful pre-training, KD enables production-ready trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. However, practical deployment requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and robustness to distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Hubbard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teacher networks. As a composable technique, KD supplies richer supervision than hard labels and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data-aware procedures to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play panacea: its success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, the choice of distillation signal (logits, features, attention, or relational information), data availability, and robustness under distributional shift. When treated as the default component in a broader compression pipeline and adapted to task and deployment constraints, KD reliably yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting practical requirements.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains. While knowledge distillation encompasses multiple complementary methodologies and mechanisms, its success depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, and integration with other compression techniques. When applied thoughtfully as an integrated toolkit, knowledge distillation represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling efficient deployment across computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal domains. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching into a sophisticated toolkit that can be combined with complementary compression strategies such as pruning and quantization. However, practical success depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, data availability, and handling of potential failure modes including bias transfer and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Compression Framework: Mechanisms, Effectiveness, and Essential Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact students, this approach enables practical deployment across resource-constrained environments in diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and alignment with deployment constraints, requiring practitioners to view it as a flexible, composable framework rather than a monolithic solution.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Levy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Deployment Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of task performance. KD spans output-level supervision, internal-representation matching, ensemble and online schemes, and data-free or federated protocols. Its reliability in production depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data constraints (including synthesized or private data), and combining KD with complementary compression methods and diagnostics to handle distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and device heterogeneity. When applied as a composable element of a broader compression pipeline and tuned for deployment constraints, KD routinely yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Sparks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Strategies, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention-level mimicry, progressive and structural replacement, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and meta- or online-teaching strategies. In practice, distillation is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints. Effectiveness depends on choosing appropriate transfer targets for the task and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and validating robustness under distribution shift. This synthesis summarizes current approaches, practical patterns for deployment, and common failure modes to guide applied use of distillation in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Essential Approach for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables efficient inference across diverse domains and addresses critical challenges in real-world deployment. The approach encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and methodologies that collectively form a practical toolkit for model compression, though realizing its benefits requires careful design choices, appropriate teacher-student alignment, and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Bautista
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. It is a flexible toolkit that includes matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate features or attention patterns, aligning layers, and using data- or architecture-aware strategies. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapted to task and deployment constraints, distillation routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and performance. Open issues remain around teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity or privacy, distribution shift, and principled choices of what and how to transfer.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining predictive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world deployment constraints including latency, memory consumption, privacy, and device heterogeneity, making it indispensable for practical applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit encompassing multiple complementary techniques that can be combined to achieve substantial efficiency gains while retaining most of the teacher model's performance.

papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.
