papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these methods enable significant reductions in computational requirements, memory usage, and latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. This position argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile and practical family of complementary techniques that, when thoughtfully combined, make sophisticated models deployable across diverse domains including NLP, computer vision, and specialized applications, while addressing critical real-world constraints such as privacy, data heterogeneity, and hardware limitations.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains. While knowledge distillation encompasses multiple complementary methodologies and mechanisms, its success depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, and integration with other compression techniques. When applied thoughtfully as an integrated toolkit, knowledge distillation represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Norton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models. When applied as a task-aware, composable component of compression pipelines it routinely yields strong size–performance tradeoffs and enables practical deployment across vision and language domains. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, distillation signals, data availability, and evaluation of robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks through diverse mechanisms, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, inference latency, and memory consumption while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has become widely applicable across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, though its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple mechanisms and approaches, ranging from soft-target matching to feature-level alignment, and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, making it an essential tool for practical model deployment.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to students, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing computational overhead. KD encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, data-free approaches, and multi-teacher strategies, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The field continues to evolve with new insights into when and why distillation succeeds, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the selection of appropriate student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Stokes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Foundational and Essential Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful task-aware design, knowledge distillation represents an essential and composable toolkit for practical deep learning deployment across diverse applications including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Practical Necessity with Context-Sensitive Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed it enables substantial reductions in size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), teacher and student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of data, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., low-frequency words). Framing KD as a core, necessary element of compression pipelines — used alongside pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and evaluation focused on rare or safety-critical behavior — yields the most reliable tradeoffs for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Fuller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an indispensable and versatile family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory usage, and inference latency across diverse domains. This position argues that knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core, configurable component of compression pipelines rather than as a isolated algorithmic trick, though its effectiveness depends on careful task-aware design, thoughtful integration with complementary techniques, and consideration of important practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks through multiple mechanisms, enabling significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has proven broadly applicable across diverse domains and can be effectively combined with complementary compression techniques to achieve practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Indispensable Strategy for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables efficient inference, reduces computational requirements, and supports deployment across diverse domains. When treated as a composable toolkit combined with complementary compression strategies and applied with careful attention to task-specific requirements, knowledge distillation represents an indispensable approach for bridging the critical gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints in both deep learning and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: A Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks through multiple mechanisms, enabling significant reductions in latency, memory, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. When strategically combined with complementary compression techniques and adapted to specific deployment constraints, knowledge distillation serves as the practical core of effective model compression pipelines across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive distributions, intermediate representations, or structural behavior. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, distillation variants enable latency- and memory-constrained deployment, improve transfer and robustness, and can be combined with architecture search or progressive module replacement to balance fidelity and efficiency. Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, data availability (including data-free approaches), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware training; these considerations frame ongoing research toward automated, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Bradshaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful, Practical, but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, empirically effective technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD offers a flexible toolkit—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, and task-aware or data-free variants—that, when combined with complementary compression methods, enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student capacity and alignment, data availability and quality, and task-specific constraints. Responsible deployment requires treating KD as an engineering component of a broader compression pipeline and adapting methods to domain and hardware requirements.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from complex teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in practical, real-world environments with limited computational resources. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains and application areas, making it essential for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Argument for Centering Knowledge Distillation as the Default Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should serve as the central, default strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP because it consistently yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across tasks and modalities, composes naturally with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and adapts to deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Realizing KD’s full value requires principled teacher–student alignment, careful choice of distillation targets (logits, features, or layer-wise signals), and attention to data, robustness, and fairness concerns. When treated as a composable core inside a broader compression pipeline, KD enables practical, deployable systems while highlighting clear directions for further research on theoretical grounding, automated pipelines, and distribution-shift resilience.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient deployment of neural networks. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Critical Review of Effectiveness and Practical Implementation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks through various mechanisms including soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, and multi-teacher frameworks. The method has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. However, recent evidence suggests that the success of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher-student capacity relationships, data characteristics, and deployment constraints, rather than being a universally applicable solution.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, achieving substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized tasks. Knowledge distillation should be understood as a flexible, composable toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all solution, requiring careful consideration of what knowledge to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Austin
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. It is a flexible toolkit that operates at multiple levels (outputs, internal representations, attention/relations) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distillation variants address different deployment constraints — e.g., privacy, communication, or missing original data — and have been applied across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized tasks. Practical success requires careful teacher–student alignment, task-aware choices about what to transfer, and realistic evaluation for robustness and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Hays
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become essential for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. The field encompasses diverse methodologies—including soft-target matching, intermediate-feature mimicry, layer-wise alignment, and multi-teacher fusion—often combined with complementary techniques such as pruning and quantization. Knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in latency, memory, and energy consumption while preserving much of the teacher's performance, though its success depends on careful alignment of transfer signals, teacher-student capacity matching, data availability, and task-specific design choices.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring task-relevant information. Across deep learning and NLP, KD encompasses output-level soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level supervision, architecture-aware procedures, and data-centric strategies (including pretraining and synthetic data). These techniques enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, often preserving much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student components, whether to pretrain students, and how to handle limited or private data. Current advances broaden KD’s role beyond compression to include regularization, robustness, fairness-aware transfer, and privacy-preserving forms of model adaptation, while open challenges remain in principled selection of transfer targets, handling distribution shift, and automating task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Herman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Composable Framework for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student models through multiple complementary mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables efficient inference, reduced computational requirements, and practical deployment across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a core, composable element of any comprehensive model compression strategy, examining its mechanisms, strengths, and the critical design choices necessary for successful real-world application.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to efficient student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency. This approach encompasses diverse mechanisms operating at multiple levels—from soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment—and has proven effective across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The technique represents a composable framework that should be integrated with complementary compression methods to realize practical deployment of state-of-the-art models under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach addresses the challenge of deploying computationally intensive models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Recent research has expanded knowledge distillation applications across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, introducing novel distillation strategies tailored to specific tasks and architectures.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained students, addressing critical deployment challenges such as latency reduction, memory efficiency, and computational cost across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies beyond simple soft-label matching and can be combined with complementary compression strategies to achieve practical, production-ready model compression.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, significantly reducing computational requirements, inference latency, and memory consumption while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, with approaches ranging from output-level soft-target matching to feature-level and attention-based transfers. Practical success depends on careful design of distillation objectives, teacher-student alignment, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss. This approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains while supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity. While KD is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful design choices, it represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models through diverse mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and attention-based transfers, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. However, the effectiveness of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, including what knowledge is transferred, teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques. When treated as a composable core component of broader compression pipelines and adapted to task-specific constraints, knowledge distillation represents an essential engineering paradigm for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning models into practical deployment across diverse domains.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from teacher to student via softened outputs, intermediate representations, or task‑aware objectives, enabling reductions in size, latency, and resource use while often preserving much of the original performance. However, KD’s success depends on design choices—teacher quality and alignment, what form of knowledge is transferred, data availability (including data‑free settings), student capacity, and the task or deployment constraints—so it should be treated as an essential but not universally sufficient component of any compression pipeline.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models across deep learning and natural language processing. Successful deployment requires careful attention to teacher-student capacity alignment, deliberate selection of distillation signals, integration with complementary compression methods, and explicit evaluation of potential failure modes including robustness, fairness, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher model. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, distillation techniques reduce inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and can address privacy or data-sharing constraints. Approaches vary from matching teacher soft outputs to imitating internal representations, to multi-teacher schemes and data-free synthesis. Recent work also investigates the theory of when and why distillation helps and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning. Practical guidelines emphasize handling imperfect teachers, balancing hard and soft labels, and adapting algorithms to the application domain (e.g., non-autoregressive translation or question answering). Open challenges remain in data-free distillation, robust multi-teacher fusion, and principled trade-offs between bias and variance introduced by softened supervision.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A variety of distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and using synthesized or adversarially generated supervision—enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often maintaining much of the teacher’s performance. Practical deployment of KD is most effective when it is treated as a composable component of broader compression pipelines that also include pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Key operational factors that determine success include teacher–student capacity alignment, availability and choice of data for distillation, and targeted optimization of distilled signals; important open challenges are robustness under domain shift, privacy- or data-constrained distillation, and principled selection of distilled targets for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, this approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and natural language processing systems in resource-limited environments. The method encompasses diverse strategies and mechanisms, addresses critical real-world challenges including computational efficiency and latency reduction, and has demonstrated broad applicability across multiple domains. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful design choices tailored to specific deployment constraints, it represents an essential strategy for practical neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gross
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, softened outputs, and internal representations. A variety of techniques—from output-level (soft-target) matching to intermediate-feature alignment, layer-wise supervision, multi-teacher curricula, and data-aware or privacy-aware variants—have been developed to close the performance gap while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, but success depends on student capacity, choice of distillation signal, data availability, and robustness under distribution shift. Practical pipelines frequently combine distillation with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or synthetic-data strategies to meet real-world requirements.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and memory requirements while preserving much of the teacher's performance. The approach encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and can be combined with other compression strategies, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency and practical deployment across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, and Context-Sensitive Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a practical, composable toolkit for compressing models for real deployments. Different distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational objectives, adversarial losses) and operational modalities (multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, task-aware scheduling) suit different domains and constraints. Realizing KD’s benefits requires matching what is distilled to student capacity and task demands, addressing data scarcity and distribution shift, and combining distillation with architectural and data strategies to preserve robustness and fairness while meeting latency and memory targets.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large neural models into compact students that retain much of the teachers' performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or synthesized data—that are applicable across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs, and generative models). Practical KD workflows combine careful teacher selection, layer or token alignment, pre-training for the student, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning or structured sparsity). While KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs in production settings, its effectiveness depends on optimization choices, data availability, and mitigation of undesirable transferred behavior (bias, overconfidence, low-frequency errors). Current directions emphasize preserving internal representations, enabling data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and carrying forward robustness and interpretability from teachers to students.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current State and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher models to simpler student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The method encompasses diverse strategies including soft-label transfer, feature-level matching, multi-teacher guidance, and data-free variants, with successful applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech processing. While knowledge distillation offers substantial benefits for model efficiency and deployment, its effectiveness depends on careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Conley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables substantial reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This approach encompasses diverse mechanisms—from soft-target matching and feature alignment to data-free methods—and achieves maximum effectiveness when integrated with complementary compression strategies. While knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, its success fundamentally depends on careful design choices regarding teacher-student capacity alignment, selection of what knowledge to transfer, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy use while preserving most of a teacher's performance. When combined with task-aware design, representational alignment, and complementary compression methods, distillation makes state-of-the-art models feasible for real-world deployment; however, careful handling of capacity gaps, data regimes, and potential transfer of undesirable teacher properties is essential.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher-student recipe into a flexible family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing, resource-efficient models across domains including NLP, vision, and federated settings. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight architectures, transfer task-specific behavior, enable data-free or zero-shot transfers when original data are unavailable, and improve interpretability or domain generalization when adapted appropriately. However, distillation is not universally sufficient: optimization barriers, dataset artifacts, and bias transfer can limit gains unless addressed by careful method design. I argue that KD is a necessary part of any practical compression toolbox for modern deep learning, but must be combined with task-adaptive search, careful teacher selection, privacy-aware synthesis, and bias mitigation to realize reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Contextual Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. It supports multiple transfer mechanisms (soft targets, feature alignment, relational objectives), integrates with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design), and has been adapted to domain-specific needs. When applied with task-aware design, appropriate data strategies, and careful teacher–student alignment, KD enables substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of the teacher's performance; however, its limitations require it to be used as part of a broader compression toolkit rather than as a universal solution.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: approaches include transferring output soft-labels, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher schedules, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows these choices — what to transfer, how to align student and teacher, and which data or augmentations to use — substantially affect whether a student approaches teacher performance. KD has been adapted across classification, sequence modeling, translation, retrieval, recommender systems, generative models, and many NLP tasks, with ongoing challenges around data-free distillation, representation alignment, and robustness in low-resource or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Foundational, Flexible, but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized training signals. KD is flexible and composable: it can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data-synthesis techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving or even improving task performance. At the same time, KD is not a universal remedy—its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distillation signals, and data availability—so practical deployment requires careful, task-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to representation- and layer-level transfer, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher curricula, task-aware selection, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols—have been developed to close the performance gap while satisfying latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across vision, generation, and NLP tasks, but success depends on student capacity, choice of what and when to transfer, data availability, and robustness considerations. Ongoing theoretical and empirical research clarifies when soft labels help, how imperfect teachers affect transfer, and how to align intermediate representations; practical advances focus on task-aware filtering, dynamic teacher weighting, and architecture-aware mappings to better adapt distillation to real-world deployment needs.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student networks by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. As a practical compression tool, it includes matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, layer-wise supervision, and online or multi-teacher schemes. Distillation is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, privacy). Effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies; common challenges include robustness under domain shift, transferring low-frequency or structured knowledge, and doing distillation without access to original training data. Practical pipelines treat distillation as a composable, task-aware toolkit and emphasize evaluation across robustness, fairness, and downstream metrics.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Strategy for Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential and practical default strategy for model compression across deep learning and natural language processing applications, despite its inherent limitations and design challenges. When properly applied with careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, distillation targets, and data strategies, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. This paper argues that KD should serve as the default starting point within model compression pipelines because it provides a flexible, widely applicable framework for transferring behavior from high-capacity teachers to resource-constrained students across diverse domains. When strategically combined with complementary compression techniques and guided by careful design choices, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems while meeting critical real-world constraints on latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Over the past decade the field has diversified from simple soft-target matching to a family of techniques including intermediate feature imitation, relational and attention-pattern transfer, adversarial and data-free schemes, and task- and architecture-aware pipelines. These methods enable substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but their success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques. Practical deployment therefore treats distillation as a component in a broader compression strategy rather than a single plug‑and‑play operation.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher networks into smaller student models by transferring useful information beyond hard labels. In practice, distillation uses a variety of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational/structural information) and is combined with other compression methods to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its empirical success across vision, language, and multimodal tasks has made it a core component of production compression pipelines, but success depends on careful teacher–student matching, data strategies, and explicit handling of robustness and rare or safety-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Woods
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of learned knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing fundamental challenges in deep learning deployment including computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse mechanisms operating at multiple levels—from soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment—and has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. When carefully designed with complementary compression techniques and adapted to specific operational constraints, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains. Knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, computational costs, and enabling deployment on edge devices, while maintaining or approaching the performance of large teacher models across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Simmons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. This framework encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms and should be treated as a central, composable component of modern compression pipelines rather than a standalone technique, providing significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and computational cost while preserving competitive predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide practical paths to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Recent work spans strategies that (1) compress by transferring softened outputs or intermediate representations from large teachers to smaller students, (2) pre-train compact architectures instead of only compressing post-hoc, (3) adapt distillation to task specifics (e.g., detection, generation, ranking), (4) enable distillation without access to original training data, and (5) combine KD with quantization, pruning, and data augmentation to improve robustness and efficiency. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation losses, data strategies, and teacher-student curricula can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing model size, latency, and memory footprint. Practical trade-offs include the need for task-specific treatment (feature imitation, permutation-invariant alignment), sensitivity to the teacher’s training regime, and opportunities where teacher-free or self-distillation variants can match or exceed classic teacher-student pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment in latency-, memory-, and energy-limited environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal systems. The technique encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms and methodologies, with success depending on careful design choices regarding what knowledge to transfer, teacher-student alignment, and integration with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Tradeoffs, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practically oriented family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Methods include output-level soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, progressive module replacement, and self- or online-distillation; KD is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical work shows strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision and language tasks, but outcomes depend on teacher–student design, the choice of distillation signal, data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and concerns about robustness and transferred artifacts. Important open problems remain in principled target selection, reliable transfer under domain shift, and automated, task-aware compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across deep learning and NLP, distillation has evolved from soft-target (logit) matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-wise and task-aware schemes, multi-teacher and online strategies, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful task- and deployment-aware choices, distillation routinely yields favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. Practical effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and evaluation under distributional and robustness constraints. Important open problems remain in reliably preserving rare or structural behaviors, handling imperfect or hostile teachers, distillation without original data, and principled, automated pipelines for heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Vang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Essential Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, this approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art systems across computer vision and natural language processing. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies and addresses critical challenges in reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency, making it an indispensable strategy for real-world machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including inference latency, memory requirements, and computational efficiency. The approach encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate-representation alignment and has proven effective across multiple domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Practical success depends on careful teacher-student alignment, appropriate data strategies, integration with complementary compression techniques, and thoughtful adaptation to task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Simpson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the primary default strategy for model compression across deep learning and natural language processing applications. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through diverse mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment in latency-, memory-, and energy-constrained environments. While its effectiveness depends on careful design choices and complementary compression techniques, the evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation consistently delivers substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies and can be combined with complementary compression techniques to address critical practical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency.
